# BPCS Interlock Specification Template

## Design rules for using the template

These rules address your three goals.

1. **No numeric setpoints in the interlock sheet.** Every trip value, reset value, deadband, and timer is referenced by a **Setpoint Register key** such as `PT-1105.TRIP_LO`. The value lives only in the Setpoint Register, which is your MOC-controlled Alarm & Trip Schedule. Instrument ranges stay in the instrument index. If someone writes a number into the sheet, the sheet is wrong.
2. **Every line gets a stable ID** (C1, E1, R1, AC-3 …). The configurer implements against these IDs, and FAT steps trace back to them.
3. **Acceptance criteria (Section 11) are written as testable statements.** Each one is one stimulus and one observable result. The FAT team turns each AC into a test step without interpretation.
4. **The FAT record captures the values.** At test time, the tester records the Setpoint Register revision and the values read from the configured system. The test record is a record, not a spec, so the value appears there legitimately.
5. **Unknowns are marked `TBC` with an owner.** No sheet goes to "Issued for Configuration" with open TBCs in Sections 3–8.

---

## Template

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BPCS INTERLOCK SPECIFICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Interlock ID:            [unit]-IL-[nnn]
Title:                   [short functional description]
Unit / Area:             
Revision / Date:         
Status:                  Draft | Issued for Review | Issued for Configuration
                         | As-Tested (FAT) | As-Built
Responsible engineer:    
Setpoint Register rev referenced:  [register doc no.] Rev [x]
```

### 1. Classification and boundary

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Function type | BPCS interlock / permissive / sequence step |
| Is this a SIF in the SRS? | **Must be "No"**. If yes, stop: it belongs in the SRS. |
| Credited as BPCS IPL in LOPA? | Yes / No. If yes, give the LOPA ref and confirm independence from the initiating cause. |
| Related SIS / BMS functions | [SIF IDs, BMS trip IDs on the same hazard] |
| HAZOP / LOPA references | |
| Legacy source documents | [old logic sheet no., C&E drawing no. & rev, old DCS block/point names] |

- **Hazard / consequence protected against:**
- **Intended action in one sentence:**

### 3. Initiators (causes)

| ID | Tag | Service | Condition | Trip SP key | Reset / hysteresis key | Delay key | Bad-PV action |

| C1 | | | < / > / = state | | | | Trip / Alarm only / Hold last |

**Voting / combination logic:** [e.g. C1 OR C2; 1oo1; 2oo3]

## Filled example: Heater low fuel gas pressure

> **Classification flag:** On many fired heaters, low fuel gas pressure is a BMS/SIS trip per API 556 or local practice. Check whether it is a SIF in your SRS before using this as a BPCS sheet. This example **assumes** the SRS contains a separate low-low trip on an independent transmitter, and that PT-1105 / XV-1106 is a non-credited BPCS layer. Unit/heater numbers (Unit 11, H-1101) and all `TBC` items are illustrative.

```
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
BPCS INTERLOCK SPECIFICATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Interlock ID:            11-IL-014
Title:                   H-1101 Low Fuel Gas Pressure – Close Main Fuel Valve
Unit / Area:             Unit 11 – Crude Heater H-1101
Revision / Date:         A / 2026-10-18
Status:                  Draft
Responsible engineer:    [name]
Setpoint Register rev referenced:  [ATS-11-001] Rev [TBC]
```

### 1. Classification and boundary

| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Function type | BPCS interlock |
| Is this a SIF in the SRS? | No (confirm against SRS: see open item O1) |
| Credited as BPCS IPL in LOPA? | No |
| Related SIS / BMS functions | SIF [TBC] on PT-1105B low-low (SRS); BMS heater trip |
| HAZOP / LOPA references | HAZOP node [TBC], deviation "Less pressure – fuel gas" |
| Legacy source documents | Logic sheet [TBC]; C&E drawing [TBC] Rev [TBC]; legacy points PT1105, XV1106, [logic block TBC] |

### 2. Purpose

- **Hazard / consequence:** Low fuel gas pressure at the burners can cause flame instability or flame-out, with risk of unburnt fuel accumulating in the firebox and re-ignition.
- **Intended action:** On sustained low fuel gas pressure downstream of the control valve, close the main fuel gas shutoff valve XV-1106 and hold it closed until reset.

### 3. Initiators

| ID | Tag | Service | Condition | Trip SP key | Reset / hysteresis key | Delay key | Bad-PV action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PT-1105 | H-1101 main fuel gas pressure, downstream of PV-1105 | PV < trip SP | `PT-1105.TRIP_LO` | `PT-1105.TRIP_LO_DB` | `PT-1105.TRIP_LO_DLY` | Trip (fail-safe), TBC with Operations (O2) |
| C2 | PT-1105 | Same | Signal quality BAD (out of range, open circuit, comms fault) | — | — | `PT-1105.BADPV_DLY` | Trip, per C1 decision |

**Voting:** C1 OR C2 (1oo1 on PT-1105).

### 4. Permissives and conditions

| ID | Condition | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Interlock is armed only when the heater is "in service" (BMS main-flame-proven signal TRUE) | Prevents a standing trip during cold start and lighting. Low pressure before main flame is managed by the BMS light-off sequence. TBC (O3) |

### 5. Actions

| ID | Tag | Final element | Action on trip | Fail position | Position feedback | Discrepancy alarm / timer key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | XV-1106 | Main fuel gas shutoff valve, H-1101 | Close (de-energize solenoid XY-1106) | Closed (fail-close) | ZSC-1106 (closed), ZSO-1106 (open) | `XV-1106.TRAVEL_TMR` |

**Associated control actions:**
- E2: PIC-1105 (fuel gas pressure controller) forced to MANUAL, output to the value held by `PIC-1105.TRIP_OUT`. This prevents integral windup while the valve is closed and gives a controlled relight.
- E3: TIC-11xx (coil outlet temperature, cascade master to fuel gas) forced out of cascade / to tracking. Tag TBC (O4).
- **Not affected:** pilot gas supply (separate line). Confirm (O5).

### 6. Latching and reset

| ID | Item | Entry |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Latching? | Yes |
| R2 | Reset type | Manual, operator HMI reset button on H-1101 overview |
| R3 | Reset permitted only when | C1 and C2 clear (PT-1105 > `PT-1105.TRIP_LO` + `PT-1105.TRIP_LO_DB`, quality GOOD) **and** no BMS trip active |
| R4 | After reset | XV-1106 remains closed. Opening requires a separate operator open command via the BMS relight permissive. |
| R5 | Restart dependencies | BMS relight sequence (purge per BMS logic, not this interlock) |

### 7. Bypass / override

| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| Bypass permitted? | Yes, for maintenance of PT-1105 only, TBC (O6) |
| Bypass method | HMI soft bypass on interlock faceplate |
| Authorization level | Shift supervisor login |
| Bypass indication & alarm | A4, persistent banner on H-1101 overview |
| Max bypass time | Auto-removed after `11-IL-014.BYP_MAX` |
| Logging | Event journal and site bypass register |

### 8. Alarms and HMI

| ID | Alarm / indication | Point | Priority | SP key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Fuel gas pressure low (pre-alarm) | PT-1105 PVLO | Medium | `PT-1105.ALM_LO` | Must be above trip SP |
| A2 | Low fuel gas pressure interlock tripped | 11-IL-014 | High | — | |
| A3 | First-out | 11-IL-014 FO | — | — | Distinguishes C1 vs C2 |
| A4 | Interlock bypassed | 11-IL-014 BYP | Medium | — | |
| A5 | XV-1106 failed to close | XV-1106 DISC | High | `XV-1106.TRAVEL_TMR` | ZSC not made within timer after E1 command |

**Display(s):** H-1101 Overview; Unit 11 Interlock Summary.

### 9. Interfaces

| Interfaces with | Description |
|---|---|
| BMS | Input: main-flame-proven (P1). Output: interlock-tripped status to BMS (TBC whether required). |
| SIS | None directly; independent low-low trip on PT-1105B in SRS. |
| Other BPCS interlocks | [TBC: e.g. heater pass low flow interlock also closes XV-1106; check for shared reset] |

### 10. Migration notes

| # | Note | Action / owner |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Legacy C&E shows a trip delay that is not present in the logic printout | Field-verify the as-found legacy config before cutover. Register value governs. [owner] |
| M2 | Legacy bad-PV behaviour undocumented | Decide per O2. Record as deliberate change if different. |
| M3 | New DCS: confirm how BAD quality propagates through the comparator block and what the interlock does on controller download / cold restart (must not open XV-1106) | Configurer |

### 11. Acceptance criteria

| AC | Precondition | Stimulus | Expected result | Traces to |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AC-1 | P1 TRUE, XV-1106 open, no bypass | Ramp PT-1105 down to just above `TRIP_LO` | A1 activates at `ALM_LO`. No trip. | A1 |
| AC-2 | As AC-1 | Ramp PT-1105 below `TRIP_LO` and hold for less than `TRIP_LO_DLY` | No trip | C1 |
| AC-3 | As AC-1 | Hold PT-1105 below `TRIP_LO` for longer than `TRIP_LO_DLY` | XV-1106 commanded closed. A2 activates. A3 shows C1. | C1, E1, A2, A3 |
| AC-4 | After AC-3 | Observe controllers | PIC-1105 in MAN at `TRIP_OUT`. TIC out of cascade. | E2, E3 |
| AC-5 | After AC-3 | Simulate ZSC-1106 not made | A5 activates after `TRAVEL_TMR` | A5 |
| AC-6 | Tripped, PT-1105 still low | Press reset | Reset rejected. Interlock stays tripped. | R3 |
| AC-7 | Tripped, PT-1105 above `TRIP_LO` but within deadband | Press reset | Reset rejected | R3 |
| AC-8 | Tripped, PT-1105 above `TRIP_LO` + `TRIP_LO_DB` | Press reset | Interlock resets. XV-1106 **stays closed**. | R1, R4 |
| AC-9 | Armed, healthy | Force PT-1105 to BAD quality longer than `BADPV_DLY` | Trip as AC-3. A3 shows C2. | C2 |
| AC-10 | P1 FALSE | PT-1105 below `TRIP_LO` | No trip | P1 |
| AC-11 | Armed | Apply bypass, then drop PT-1105 below trip | No trip. A4 active. Event logged. | Sec. 7 |
| AC-12 | Bypass applied | Wait `BYP_MAX` | Bypass auto-removed. Alarm/log entry created. | Sec. 7 |
| AC-13 | XV-1106 closed, interlock reset | Controller download / restart | XV-1106 remains closed. No spurious open command. | M3 |

### 12. Open items

| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Confirm this function is not a SIF in the SRS | Safety | |
| O2 | Bad-PV = trip or alarm only | Operations / Process | |
| O3 | Confirm P1 arming condition | Process / BMS vendor | |
| O4 | Confirm COT controller tag and cascade behaviour | Control systems | |
| O5 | Confirm pilots are unaffected by XV-1106 | Process | |
| O6 | Confirm bypass permitted | Operations | |

---

## How AC-3 becomes a FAT step

This shows goal (b) in practice.

| Step | Action | Expected | Recorded value | Pass/Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11-IL-014 / AC-3 | Set PT-1105 sim to [trip SP from Register rev __] minus 5% span and hold | XV-1106 close command after [delay from Register] ± 1 scan. A2 on. First-out = C1. | Register rev: __ / TRIP_LO read from config: __ / Delay read: __ / Measured delay: __ | |

The tester confirms that the configured value equals the Register value. This also catches setpoint drift between the register and the configuration.

---

## Practical tips for 40 units

- **Make the Setpoint Register keys the actual DCS parameter paths** where the platform allows, e.g. `PT-1105.TRIP_LO` maps directly to a block parameter. Then a configuration export can be diffed automatically against the register, and the comparison becomes a script instead of a manual check.
- **Keep the sheets in a structured format** (spreadsheet or database, one row per C/E/AC line) rather than Word. You can then generate the C&E matrix, the bypass list, and the FAT procedure from the same source.
- **Add a "classification check" signature (Section 13) on every sheet.** During migrations, functions that should be in the SIS often turn up in BPCS logic. Low fuel gas pressure on heaters is a classic example.
